requested.title: LLM relay follows unvalidated redirects and re-resolves user-controlled endpoints

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The finding accurately described the older code path, but the current target file no longer performs a bare fetch to the user-controlled provider URL. deploy/self-hosted/agent-runner.mjs now imports assertPublicHttpUrl and requestPublicUrl from deploy/self-hosted/agent-runner-egress.mjs, validates the computed /chat/completions URL when /llm is configured, and uses requestPublicUrl for the relay POST. The egress helper resolves the hostname itself, rejects localhost, .localhost, .local, private, link-local, reserved, multicast, IPv4 legacy forms, and IPv6 transition forms, and rejects the whole hostname if any DNS answer is private. Its pinnedRequest passes a custom lookup function to node:http/node:https so the socket connects only to the exact address that passed validation, preventing DNS rebinding between validation and connection. Redirects are handled manually rather than by fetch: each 3xx Location is parsed, sensitive headers are stripped on cross-origin redirects, and the next URL is passed back through assertPublicHttpUrl before another request is opened. The test file scripts/agent-runner-egress.test.mjs includes explicit coverage for private redirects, mixed public-private redirect DNS answers, and public redirect hops being revalidated and pinned. Git history confirms commit 7358441c replaced fetch(relay.url) with requestPublicUrl(relay.url) and added the runner-side registration validation. A user can still choose a generic BYOK base URL, but the concrete redirect-to-internal-service and DNS-rebinding attack scenario described in this finding is blocked in the runner itself.
